question: Which of the following antitubercular drugs can be safely used in severe renal failure :
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Streptomycin" -> "aminoglycoside antibiotic" -> "excreted by kidneys" -> "accumulates in renal failure" -> "not safe in severe renal failure" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Ethambutol" -> "excreted by kidneys" -> "accumulates in renal failure" -> "dose adjustment needed" -> "not safe without adjustment" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Capreomycin" -> "aminoglycoside-like antibiotic" -> "excreted by kidneys" -> "accumulates in renal failure" -> "not safe in severe renal failure" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Rifampicin" -> "metabolized by liver" -> "minimal renal excretion" -> "safe in severe renal failure" -> 90%
analysis: In the context of severe renal failure, the safety of antitubercular drugs is primarily determined by their excretion pathways. Streptomycin and Capreomycin are aminoglycoside or aminoglycoside-like antibiotics that are primarily excreted by the kidneys. This makes them unsafe in severe renal failure without dose adjustment due to the risk of accumulation and toxicity. Ethambutol is also excreted by the kidneys and requires dose adjustment, thus it is not safe without modification. Rifampicin, on the other hand, is primarily metabolized by the liver and has minimal renal excretion, making it the safest option among the listed drugs for use in severe renal failure. This aligns with standard medical knowledge and consensus, supporting the choice of Rifampicin as the most appropriate drug in this scenario.
